name: [R26] Linux kernel UAF/KASAN crash near TCP SYN/SYNACK handling (CVE-2026-98432)
message:
Exploratory heuristic for CVE-2026-98432 (Ubuntu priority High, CVSS 3.1 9.8/Critical): a use-after-free in the Linux kernel's IPv4 TCP SYN/SYNACK path. When a retransmitted SYN is processed on another CPU, the SYNACK path can read IP options already handed to a child socket and freed with plain kfree() instead of kfree_rcu(), causing a UAF in ip_options_build(). A related path exists via request-socket migration (net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req=1, or a BPF_SK_REUSEPORT_SELECT_OR_MIGRATE program). As of 2026-10-28 Ubuntu lists every supported release as "Vulnerable (work in progress)" -- no fixed package exists yet.

A kernel memory-safety bug leaves no reliable userspace log line by itself, so this looks for the kernel's own crash signature: a KASAN/UAF report (or general oops/panic) whose nearby lines name the functions this CVE implicates (tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock, tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor, inet_sock_destruct, ip_options_build). Requires the crash to actually surface (e.g. a KASAN-instrumented kernel) -- a miss proves nothing, a hit is a lead not proof.

Confirm kernel version and sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req with scripts/linux_kernel_cve202698432_check.py and Ubuntu's own advisory before attributing a hit to this CVE specifically.

queries.name: kernel_uaf_near_tcp_syn_functions
queries.query: source:kernel ("BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free" OR "BUG: KASAN:" OR "Kernel panic" OR "general protection fault") AND ("tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock" OR "tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor" OR "inet_sock_destruct" OR "ip_options_build")
